question.worked_solution:
To remove the radical $\sqrt{2}$ from the denominator, all we need to do is multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{2}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{45}}{\sqrt{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{45}}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{45}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{45}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Next, we notice that $45$ has a perfect square factor $(9).$ Therefore, we can rewrite $\sqrt{45}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{45} & = \\ \sqrt{9\cdot 5} & = \\ \sqrt{9}\cdot \sqrt{5} & = \\ 3\sqrt{5} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify our original fraction as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{45}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{2} & = \\ \frac{3\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{2} & = \\ \frac{3\sqrt{5\cdot 2}}{2} & = \\ \frac{3\sqrt{10}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
